name: Markets with tight spreads
summary: Read live order books and find outcomes where buying and selling cost almost the same.
description:
The spread is the gap between the best price someone will pay for an outcome (the bid) and the best price someone will sell it for (the ask). A small spread means you can trade in and out without losing much to the gap.

This workflow reads the order books of 30 markets, keeps the outcomes whose spread is under 2 cents, and lists the deepest books first.

- Run it, then open the Output of Order books to see bids, asks and depth for every outcome.
- Change the Value in Tight spreads only to be stricter or looser.
- Depth is how many shares rest on the best five price levels: a deep book takes large orders without moving.

nodes.notes: Starts the workflow when you press Run.
Lists 30 open markets, one item each.
Reads each outcome's order book: best bid, best ask, the spread between them and the depth. One item per outcome, so a Yes/No market becomes two.

nodes.name: Tight spreads only
nodes.notes: Keeps outcomes whose spread is under 0.02, that is 2 cents on the dollar. A book with only one side has no spread and is dropped.

nodes.name: Deepest first
nodes.notes: Sorts by the shares waiting on the buy side and keeps ten.
